outputs.explanation: The scatter plot explicitly shows each of the 141 individual sample measurements as separate markers; the marginal histograms are built directly from these same individual points.
Each point represents the mean ± s.d. across 6 (or fewer) replicate samples per reporter/cell line, but the individual replicate measurements underlying each averaged point/error bar are not shown.

The panel shows fitted normal distribution curves of subtype-averaged periods and amplitudes (each based on only n=1-4 cell-line averages), but the individual cell-line data points that generated each curve are not plotted, obscuring the very low underlying sample sizes.
The boxplots have individual sample data points (colored dots for Per2-Luc and Bmal1-Luc reporters) overlaid on top of the box-and-whisker summaries.

These are polar histograms built from time-resolved phase-difference values; as histograms they already visualize the full data distribution rather than a single average statistic, so an additional individual-points overlay is not required.

Like panel E, this is a histogram-type display of phase-difference distributions (aggregated by subtype), which inherently conveys the data distribution rather than a bare average, so individual-point overlay is not required.
This panel shows a single illustrative example signal trace and its fit, not an averaged/aggregated statistic, so individual data points are not applicable.
Each of the 117 samples is plotted individually as its own marker; the error bars reflect fitting uncertainty for each individual sample rather than averaging across samples.
